headline: North Woods Launch and State Park Registration
reservation: While the lake itself is open, campsites at Lily Bay State Park often fill months in advance for the summer season. The Mount Kineo shuttle is a seasonal private service that does not take reservations; visitors pay the operator directly at the Rockwood dock. Always check official Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands notices for water safety or trail closures before arrival.

days.title: Island Peaks and Flint Cliffs

stops.name: Mount Kineo State Park
stops.detail: Take the ferry to this peninsula to see the 700-foot rhyolite cliffs rising from the water.

stops.name: Kineo Fire Tower
stops.detail: Hike the Indian Trail to the summit for a 360-degree view of the Maine Highlands.

days.driving: Local shuttle boat transfer; allow 4–5 hours for the island visit.
days.note: The shuttle schedule is seasonal and weather-dependent; confirm the last return trip.

days.title: Shorelines and Wildlife Coves

stops.name: Lily Bay State Park
stops.detail: Explore the pebble beaches and the two-mile shore path for views of the distant mountains.

stops.name: Roach River Inlet
stops.detail: Visit these marshy edges in the early morning for a chance to spot moose feeding in the shallows.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for the lakeside drive; conditions vary on gravel sections.
days.note: Maintain a safe distance from all wildlife and use binoculars for observation.

days.title: North Woods History

stops.name: Moosehead Historical Society
stops.detail: Learn about local family history and Victorian life at the Eveleth-Crafts-Sheridan Historical House.

stops.name: Katahdin Steamship
stops.detail: Board the historic vessel for a narrated cruise to understand the lake's geography from the water.

days.driving: Local Greenville walking and short drives; allow 3 hours for the cruise.
days.note: The steamship operates on a specific seasonal schedule; verify departure days.

intel.title: Rockwood Boat Launch
intel.text: Parking for the Kineo shuttle is available at the public landing in Rockwood. During July and August, spaces near the dock fill quickly, necessitating a short walk from overflow areas.

intel.title: Wilderness Dead Zones
intel.text: Signal is generally reliable in Greenville but disappears quickly as you move north toward Kokadjo. Carry physical maps if you plan to explore the gravel logging roads.

intel.title: Greenville Hub
intel.text: Greenville is the primary source for fuel and groceries in the region. If heading north toward the Golden Road, ensure your tank is full before leaving the town limits.

intel.title: Moose Activity Windows
intel.text: The best viewing occurs at dawn and dusk when moose are most active near water. Suggested viewing times do not guarantee sightings, as these are wild animals in a vast habitat.

intel.title: Logging Road Protocol
intel.text: Many roads north of the lake are private logging routes. Always yield to heavy trucks and be prepared for rough, unpaved surfaces that may not be suitable for all cars.

plan.arrival: Pick up a vehicle at Bangor (BGR) and stop for outdoor supplies in Greenville before heading to your lakeside base.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are fine for main roads, but an AWD is recommended for exploring remote logging spurs; check rental terms for gravel road use.
plan.goldenHour: West Cove in Greenville; colors depend on cloud cover and seasonal smoke or haze.
